headline: Preprint reports no measurable increase in merged coding work after higher-scoring Claude model access or upgrades
summary: A new preprint uses a 19-day loss of access to Claude Fable 5 and five subsequent Claude model upgrades to study whether higher benchmark scores translated into more completed public coding work. The author reports no statistically significant change in seven-day pull-request merge rates or weekly merged pull requests. These are author-reported estimates, not an independent reproduction; the study observes public Claude Code pull requests, model attribution is sparse, and merge rates do not capture private work, time saved or all dimensions of code quality.
